facts.statement: In UVI-style raft aquaponics, the raft can treat the waste of about 180 g of fish feed per m2 of grow area per day, if solids are removed before the raft.

context.condition: solids removed upstream of the raft

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: source level E4; direct_quote; context partial
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Extension fact sheet by UVI's lead researcher. It does not say at what TAN level this applies, or whether plant ammonium uptake is included. Cross-check: Consistent with UVI's statement that the raft gives adequate biofiltration at the design feed ratio; about 10x higher per m2 than trickling-filter and RBC biofilm rates, which are not directly comparable.

facts.statement: The UVI commercial aquaponic system replaced about 1.5 percent of its water volume per day on average.

context.system: UVI coupled DWC raft, about 111 m3, 214 m2 grow area

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: E4 report by the system's developers; read from a third-party copy (tag2grow.org), not UVI-hosted.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Direct number. Undated, and the cause of the loss (evaporation, transpiration, solids discharge) is not stated.

corroboration.note: SRAC 454 says closed systems exchange less than 2 percent a day.

facts.statement: In UVI-style aquaponics, denitrification happens in anaerobic sludge on the filter-tank netting; cleaning the netting less often increases denitrification and lowers nitrate.

context.system: UVI coupled DWC raft with clarifier and orchard-netting filter tanks

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Two UVI-authored sources agree on mechanism and direction. No denitrification rate is given by either.

approval.record: Approval Batch 002, approved as recommended (thread message 2026-11-26 01:33 Europe/Amsterdam)

facts.statement: By adjusting filter-tank cleaning, nitrate-N in a UVI-style system can be held anywhere from about 1 to 100 mg/L or more.

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Stated as guidance without a cited measurement.

facts.statement: In tilapia aquaponics with tomato, basil or lettuce, about 45 to 50 percent of total N input was lost by denitrification, 14 to 20 percent left in wastewater, and 9 to 17 percent ended up in plants.

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: E3 peer-reviewed journal with DOI; abstract only, read via FAO AGRIS.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Peer-reviewed mass balance, but only the abstract was read and ranges span three crops. Scale and feed rate not known.

corroboration.note: Qualitatively consistent with UVI's account of denitrification controlling nitrate.

facts.statement: FAO small-scale aquaponics guidance sizes a media-bed biofilter at 1 L of volcanic gravel (about 300 m2/m3) per g of daily feed, or 0.5 L of bioballs (about 600 m2/m3), as a minimum; limestone gravel has about 150 to 200 m2/m3, and larger gravel gives less surface.

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: FAO Fisheries and Aquaculture Technical Paper 589, read via a third-party reproduction (FarmHub).
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Stated design minimum, not a measured capacity; read through a reproduction.
review_metadata.reviewed_from_file: web reads 2026-11-26 (gravel-bed N and basil density fixes)

facts.statement: SRAC 453 (1999) gives trickling filters a design loading of 3.6 kg feed per m3 of media per day for media generally below 330 m2/m3, with nitrification of about 90 g TAN/m3/day.

context.note: used as the analogue for intermittently wetted gravel beds

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: University extension fact sheet; the TAN rate rests on unpublished data (Losordo).
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Design criterion, not a measurement; one edition; the 2013 edition does not restate it.

facts.statement: Trickling-filter media of 164 m2/m3 removed 0.94 to 3.92 g TAN per m2 per day at 0.81 to 4.63 mg TAN/L, with removal linear in TAN up to about 2.5 mg/L.

context.system: RAS trickling filter (Norpak media) vs microbead filter

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Measured rates; the paper's table and text swap the two filter volumes; heavily loaded RAS, not aquaponics.
